headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from Cursor’s filesystem/MCP access into MemMachine’s context and APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files, clipboard, and use MCP; MemMachine also exposes an MCP server and conversational context. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from Cursor can be passed into MemMachine as instructions. The pairwise pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Cursor content is copied into MemMachine prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization
IF a shared MCP server or workspace is used to relay content between the agents
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of raw agent output between tools
Add a provenance tag to all Cursor-generated text before forwarding
Restrict MemMachine MCP inputs to structured fields only
Review any shared MCP server for instruction filtering
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and broad network egress; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and can call APIs. If Cursor forwards sensitive workspace data into MemMachine, that data can persist in MemMachine’s memory and be exposed through its API surface. Both agents’ documented surfaces support the leakage pathway.
conditions: IF Cursor sends open-file or clipboard contents into MemMachine prompts
IF MemMachine persists conversation state containing secrets or source code
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets from Cursor into MemMachine
Turn off or scope MemMachine memory for sensitive sessions
Use separate accounts or API keys for each agent
Redact clipboard contents before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git, and broad egress; MemMachine has allowlisted egress and MCP/API access. The pair can conflict on shared mutable resources if MemMachine is pointed at the same workspace or API-backed state, even though MemMachine’s write scope is not fully specified. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or shared state
IF MemMachine is configured to write back through its API or MCP server
mitigations: Run the agents in separate workspaces
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git branches per agent
Limit MemMachine to read-only access where possible
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, edits, and shell actions; MemMachine can consume conversational context and act through API/MCP. If MemMachine treats Cursor output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or persisted memory. Both profiles show an end-to-end handoff path, but no direct verification step is documented.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests Cursor output without independent verification
IF Cursor-generated facts are used to update long-term memory or trigger API actions
mitigations: Require human review before MemMachine acts on Cursor output
Ask MemMachine to restate assumptions before execution
Keep Cursor outputs in a separate draft buffer
Use explicit validation prompts for any factual claims
requires-engineering: add a verification gate between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If regulated or sensitive data is moved from Cursor into MemMachine’s persistent memory or API-backed context, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Cursor and then forwarded into MemMachine memory
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the editor workspace and MemMachine storage
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in MemMachine memory
Document a retention policy for both tools
Use synthetic or redacted data in shared workflows
Verify residency and DPA terms before deployment
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows across both systems
